A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GEPA research. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support comparison, including matching material moved or renumbered in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original optimizer comparisons on four benchmarks, candidate-selection ablations, and NPUEval and KernelBench experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds math benchmarks, additional optimizer comparisons, cross-model transfer, full-parameter GRPO evaluation, and adversarial prompt-search results.

M1.justification: The core GEPA algorithms, reflection meta-prompt, Pareto selection, and Merge procedure are retained. Section 5.2 adds a limited adversarial adaptation: reversing the reward to minimize pass@1 while constraining prompt edits to preserve the task and necessary information.

E1.justification: The main evaluation expands from four benchmarks to six by adding AIME-2025, with earlier AIME questions for optimization, and LiveBench-Math. v2 also introduces an adversarial distractor scenario on AIME. The original four benchmarks and both kernel-generation benchmarks remain.

E2.justification: v2 Table 2 adds evaluated comparisons with Trace/OptoPrime, TextGrad, and MIPROv2-No-Demos. Table 3 adds BeamSearch to the candidate-selection comparison, and Figure 11 adds full-parameter GRPO. These substantially broaden v1's comparisons with MIPROv2, LoRA-GRPO, and greedy candidate selection.

E3.justification: New protocols include math-specific splits and single-step ChainOfThought systems, Qwen-to-GPT prompt transfer, and GPT-5 Mini adversarial evaluation. The full-parameter GRPO experiment uses a separately specified two-hop HoVer system and new training settings, including eight GPUs and FSDP2; it does not replace the original three-hop comparison.

E4.justification: v2 adds a beam-search ablation testing Pareto selection, cross-model transfer analysis, and a full-parameter GRPO comparison probing the LoRA restriction. Adversarial search adds robustness testing and manual analysis of formatting failures. Existing generalization-gap, prompt-length, search-tree, and intermediate-prompt analyses are retained.

E5.justification: v2 reports five evaluations per AIME-2025 problem, including five generations per problem in the adversarial study, and specifies LiveBench's shuffle seed as 0. These are new reporting details and evaluation repetitions, not evidence of increased optimizer-run counts. Neither version provides confidence intervals or statistical significance tests.

E6.justification: The original four-task scores and kernel results are retained, while substantial new results appear. Qwen3-8B GEPA scores 32.00 on AIME versus GRPO's 38.00; transferred prompts achieve a 62.03 aggregate on GPT-4.1 Mini; adversarial prompts reduce GPT-5 Mini AIME pass@1 from 76% to 10%. Revised six-task aggregates are not same-coverage performance changes.

T1.justification: The compound-system formalization, optimization objectives in Equations 1–2, and mathematical content of Algorithms 1–4 remain equivalent. Explicitly describing GEPA's weights as frozen clarifies the existing method. No substantive new theorem, proof, or derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: The central claim that reflective prompt evolution can outperform RL with fewer rollouts is retained. The abstract revises the average GRPO advantage from 10% over four tasks to 6% over six tasks, and the introduction expands the stated applications to adversarial prompt search.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations of cross-model transfer and distractor-induced literal answer-formatting failures. It removes v1's dedicated limitations discussion, including qualifications about data-rich regimes, omitted exemplar optimization, and possible prompt/weight integration. Some existing caveats, particularly Merge budget allocation and preliminary kernel results, remain.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-release URL, monetary costs in Appendix E.3, reflection-model call counts in Table 4, and implementation details for Trace/TextGrad and full-parameter GRPO. These substantially expand reproducibility information. Much of the original setup is simply relocated to Appendix E.

R1.justification: Related-work positioning expands to verbal reflection and self-refinement, adversarial evolutionary search, and agent-policy evolution through works including Reflexion, Self-Refine, Trace, Rainbow Teaming, and Agent-Pro. APO, math-benchmark, and SkyRL references are also added; FrugalRAG and Search Wisely are removed.

P1.justification: v2 substantially condenses and rewrites the introduction, method exposition, and related work. Evaluation setup and results are consolidated, detailed settings move to Appendix E, applications are regrouped, and appendices are reordered with an outline. The limitations section is removed and an LLM-usage disclosure is added.

P2.justification: The original combined results table becomes expanded model-specific Tables 1–2; the ablation table is extended, and Figure 11 and Table 4 are added. Figure 1 replaces HoVer with an already reported IFBench panel. Revised margins, extensive figure relocation, and regrouped appendix displays substantially change presentation.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens the evidence for GEPA's comparative advantages through relevant competing optimizers, a beam-search control, cross-model transfer, and math results that expose an AIME exception. Figure 11 addresses v1's untested full-finetuning comparison, although on a separately specified two-hop HoVer system. New cost, code-access, and reflection-call disclosures improve auditability. These gains outweigh the loss of the dedicated limitations discussion, which weakens qualification of the broader claims.
